generations.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: Helmetd motorcycle AR glasses HUD concept, wide 16:9 first-person view.
Primary request: create a high-fidelity product UI mockup of NORMAL RIDING mode based on these real product features: speed, gear, simple next-turn navigation, three directional camera inputs, contextual warnings, and voice control. This is a minimal motorcycle awareness HUD, not a desktop dashboard.
Scene/backdrop: a photorealistic rider-eye view along a quiet straight suburban road in soft overcast daylight, low buildings and trees along the edges. Only a small hint of motorcycle handlebars at the bottom. No rider portrait, glasses rims, helmet border, laptop, or giant digital dashboard. The visible road is the real scene behind see-through glasses.
UI visual system: crisp off-white sans-serif typography, pale cyan reserved for navigation, thin linework, strong readable hierarchy, medium text sizes, subtle outline where needed, essentially no glow. No large translucent glass panels. Keep over 80% of the road view free of interface.
Layout: upper-left tiny wordmark 'helmetd'; upper-right a small connection glyph and battery icon with '82%'. Top center, a compact cyan right-turn arrow beside the exact two-line navigation text '800 ft' and 'Oak Street'. Low center, above the handlebars, a clean horizontally aligned readout '42' with a small 'mph', a short hairline divider, and '3' with a small 'GEAR'. Lower-right a tiny microphone icon and 'Voice ready'. Tiny discreet non-alert side-camera symbols sit near the left and right lower edges, with no large text, no warning claims, and no camera windows in this normal state.
Presentation framing: a slim white footer outside the scene reads 'HELMETD / NORMAL RIDE' at left and 'Motorcycle HUD concept' at right. Do not let the footer obscure the road.
Constraints: one realistic complete HUD state, visually elegant and calm, exact readable labels, all data illustrative. No compass, RPM dial, engine charts, chat bubble, lengthy assistant text, object boxes in the forward road view, radar, reticle, gamer health bars, fake distance or collision predictions, notification cards, sci-fi borders, decorative circles, neon glow, tiny dense paragraphs, or extra slogans.

Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: Helmetd motorcycle AR glasses HUD concept, wide 16:9 first-person view.
Primary request: create a high-fidelity product UI mockup of LEFT TURN SIGNAL / OCCUPIED BLIND SPOT mode. The rider's left turn signal opens the left camera, and a detected vehicle in that camera gets an amber warning. Show a coherent restrained motorcycle awareness interface that could accompany a minimal normal riding screen.
Scene/backdrop: a photorealistic rider-eye view along a quiet straight suburban road in soft overcast daylight, low buildings and trees along the edges. Only a small hint of motorcycle handlebars at the bottom. This road is the real scene behind see-through glasses. No visible glasses frame, helmet border, laptop, large windshield UI, or rider portrait.
UI visual system: crisp off-white sans-serif, pale cyan navigation, restrained amber for the occupied blind spot, thin clear lines and medium readable text, little to no glow. Most of the forward road remains unobstructed.
Persistent layout: upper-left tiny 'helmetd'; upper-right a small connection glyph and battery icon with '82%'. Top center, a compact muted right-turn navigation arrow beside the exact two-line text '800 ft' and 'Oak Street'. Low center, above handlebars, the steady readout '42' with small 'mph', a short hairline divider, and '3' with small 'GEAR'. The top navigation refers to a later route instruction; the activated left signal is a separate live motorcycle input.
Contextual blind-spot UI: near the left edge at mid-height, a simple amber warning triangle with the exact words 'LEFT BLIND SPOT'. Beneath it in the lower-left quadrant, one rectangular camera inset about 27% of the total image width and 23% of its height, crisp slim amber border, minimally rounded corners. Its actual camera picture shows a car beside and slightly behind the motorcycle in the left adjacent lane, as seen by a side-facing helmet camera; the car has one precise amber detection box. The inset header reads 'LEFT CAMERA', with a small green left-arrow signal glyph and the caption 'Signal on'. Below the inset, one short amber line reads 'Vehicle beside you'. A tiny microphone glyph remains at lower-right, without assistant chatter.
Presentation framing: a slim white footer outside the scene reads 'HELMETD / LEFT BLIND SPOT' at left and 'Motorcycle HUD concept' at right.
Constraints: one complete alert state, not a multi-panel comparison. Keep the center and distant forward road clear. Exactly one camera inset and one actionable warning, no additional rear/hazard banners competing with it. No driving instructions, collision probability, invented exact vehicle distance or closing speed, route painted on the pavement, forward-world detection boxes, radar, crosshairs, giant emergency overlays, sci-fi decorations, marketing copy, or extra text.
